environment: macOS, Node v26.8.1, Python 3, local Docker daemon; synthetic registry/upstream credentials and unique temporary namespaces; no production state or credentials

confirmed_causes_and_fixes.fault: Legacy launcher leaves persistent controller.lock after SIGKILL
confirmed_causes_and_fixes.before: Actual launcher worker drill failed to restart because the old launcher saw controller.lock and exited before serving the replacement.
confirmed_causes_and_fixes.after: The new launcher uses a kernel-held controller.guard under an external Python guardian. A killed controller is terminated as a process group, the guard remains held until authority ends, and a replacement starts without deleting ownership files.

confirmed_causes_and_fixes.fault: Live controller waits forever after a Docker CLI timeout when the child ignores TERM
confirmed_causes_and_fixes.before: The real DockerShardDriver.list path remained pending after the original 5-second execFile timeout; the regression failed at 7.5 seconds.
confirmed_causes_and_fixes.after: The command runner sends TERM, escalates to KILL, verifies child exit and pipe close, and reports cleanup_unproven when that cannot be proved. The regression returned in approximately 5.7 seconds.

confirmed_causes_and_fixes.fault: Delayed Docker operations can target a reused container name
confirmed_causes_and_fixes.before: The name-based stop/remove path allowed a delayed operation to mutate a replacement using the same name.
confirmed_causes_and_fixes.after: Stop and remove use the immutable 64-character container ID, and generation checks reject stale handles.

confirmed_causes_and_fixes.fault: Controller loss after dispatch can lose the acknowledgement
confirmed_causes_and_fixes.before: A restarted controller forgot the in-memory admission and redispatched the same idempotency key; the regression observed two dispatches.
confirmed_causes_and_fixes.after: A private receipt journal persists only identity hash/state. Pending becomes unknown on restart; the same key returns relay_admission_unknown and is never redispatched. Completed response bodies are not treated as durable replay data.

confirmed_causes_and_fixes.fault: A clean first supervised startup created the ownership marker but omitted the empty Docker mutation journal
confirmed_causes_and_fixes.before: The first controller could serve successfully, then a replacement failed closed because the marker existed while docker-operations.json did not.
confirmed_causes_and_fixes.after: Initial journal setup now atomically creates the empty journal before the compatibility marker; a marker without its journal remains a fail-closed unavailable-storage state. The launcher restart regression and an explicit first-start assertion pass.

confirmed_causes_and_fixes.fault: Federation workers previously had Docker restart policy while the lifecycle controller also replaced stopped workers
confirmed_causes_and_fixes.before: A worker process exit could be acted on by both Docker's restart policy and controller reconciliation, leaving two restart authorities for one resource.
confirmed_causes_and_fixes.after: Federation workers now use Docker restart policy `no`; the lifecycle controller alone retires and replaces unexpected stopped or missing workers with exponential backoff and a five-attempt ten-minute budget. The regression proves the sixth crash is contained and emits `worker_restart_budget_exhausted`.

validation.launcher_process_drill: passed; empty-registry readiness remained 503 as required
validation.worker_restart_authority_regression: passed; Docker policy `no`, controller-only replacement, five-attempt ten-minute budget and sixth-crash containment
validation.docker_lifecycle_canary: passed against galxai-relay:lifecycle-recovery with synthetic inventory; rejected worker removed, surviving worker adopted, cold rejected credential not allocated
validation.real_worker_execution: WebSocket worker fixture passed; real Docker worker execution was not used in that launcher drill
validation.documentation: npm run docs:check and npm run test:docs passed

remaining_uncertainty: The local reproductions establish failure paths and safe containment, not the causal distribution of the September 13 production intermittency.
Host reboot, Docker-daemon restart, delayed daemon startup, retained-state restoration and full/read-only state storage drills were not run and remain open under ACT-018.
The legacy controller.lock marker requires one reviewed migration archive before the new launcher can own that namespace; no automatic takeover is attempted.
No production deployment or disruptive production fault injection was performed.
